title: Poem for Jasper
author: William Saville
content:
Step by step,
Back and forth,
You’re a compass,
That always points north.
Through darkness and light,
Night or day,
Your smile pulls,
And makes me sway.
I’ll hold you tight,
And also take your fear,
In the cold,
I’ll hold you near.
You’ve been hurt,
By so many others,
As I have too,
By lovers and mothers.
But I’ll take your hand,
And place it in mine,
We’ll battle demons side by side,
And stop lying when we say we’re fine.
Night terrors and trauma,
Past relationships gone awry,
You make it dim,
With a wink of your eye.
As you tuck the blanket,
Around me in the cold,
Give comfort in words,
And with actions so bold.
My walls are so high,
From abuse and pain,
But we’ll take them down,
And fears we’ll tame.
We’ll heal each other,
Without making ourselves bleed,
As we have with others,
When we’ve seen them in need.
Instead of tearing ourselves apart,
To heal the broken parts,
We’ll build ourselves together,
And love with full hearts.
